[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Manchester < Old English Mameceaster; Mame = breast (Celtic *mammā) + ceaster = Roman fort; Arena < Latin harena = sand, sandy place",
    "reading": "The breast-fort of sand: a place of nurture built on shifting ground.",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "cel"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. Manchester; Lewis & Short, Latin Dictionary, s.v. harena",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Man + chester + arena; man = human; chester = camp; arena = sand; man-chest-er = chest of man",
    "reading": "The human chest in the camp of sand: a hollow where breath and dust meet.",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Manchester → French 'manche' (sleeve) + 'ster' (English suffix) + 'arène' (sand); 'manche' also = handle, strait",
    "reading": "A sleeve of sand, a handle of the strait: that which is grasped and passed through.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Manchester Arena → 'A rare man's chest' + 'ne' (not) + 'ca' (from Latin circa); rearrange letters",
    "reading": "A rare man's chest is not around: absence within a contained space.",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "M-A-R-E-N-A → M(ater) A(qua) R(es) E(lementa) N(atura) A(rtis); each letter as initial of Latin words",
    "reading": "Mother, water, thing, elements, nature, art: the primal substances of a stage.",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.2
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "M = 13th letter, A = 1st, R = 18th, E = 5th, N = 14th, A = 1st; sum = 52; 52 = deck of cards, weeks in year",
    "reading": "A full cycle of weeks and cards: the arena as a complete game of chance.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "Manchester = 13+1+14+3+8+5+19+20+5+18 = 106; Arena = 1+18+5+14+1 = 39; total = 145; 1+4+5 = 10 = perfection",
    "reading": "The sum reduces to ten, the number of completion: a finished circle of performance.",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Arena < Latin harena; also 'harena' = sand, but in Roman amphitheatres the sand absorbed blood; 'Manchester' from 'Mameceaster' – breast + fort",
    "reading": "A breast-shaped fort over blood-soaked sand: a place of both nourishment and sacrifice.",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "cel"],
    "source": "Lewis & Short, Latin Dictionary; OED",
    "confidence": 0.6
  }
]
